key_idea: Because the Runner may cheat, the real game state is (available squares, set of squares still consistent for the Runner, rounds left): at most 3^9 x 9 states, so solve it exhaustively and replay the winning choices.
sketch: TrapperWins(A,S,r): there is a split of S into T and S\T such that for each non-empty side X some removal i leaves no available neighbour of X, or leads to a Trapper-winning state (A\{i}, N(X) & A\{i}, r-1); r=0 with S non-empty is a Runner win. Memoise over 512x512x10. As Trapper print the winning query and then the killing square; as Runner answer with a side for which no removal wins, track the committed sets, and at the end rebuild an actual path backwards (pick any final square, then a neighbour inside each earlier committed set). Pitfalls: the Runner may stand on the removed square, queries of size 0 have no second line, handle the judge's -1 and flush every line. Interactive, so the checker cannot judge it: validated with my own interactor over 1500 random games (random and greedy cheating runner, random trapper, path consistency check) plus both statement scenarios.
